title: Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
content:
Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
Distant LOD meshes are separate NIF files, one per level, named <Name>_LOD_0.nif, <Name>_LOD_1.nif, <Name>_LOD_2.nif and kept under Meshes\LOD\ (for example Meshes\LOD\Architecture\Shacks\). Vanilla keeps their textures under Textures\LOD\ and their materials under Materials\LOD\, small and separate from the full-detail textures.
Keep them very low: across 900 vanilla LOD meshes the median _LOD_0 is 8 triangles, 90% are 125 or fewer, the largest is about 2,200 (the USS Constitution), and city buildings use roughly 150-450.
A LOD material must not point at the full-size textures: if the LOD NIF still names the object's own .bgsm, the game draws the 4K textures on every LOD, because the .bgsm overrides the textures in the NIF.
Attaching them (do NOT make a separate STAT for a LOD mesh):
1. Open the object's own STAT record, the one with the full-detail model that you place in the world.
2. Tick Has Distant LOD, click Specify distant LOD meshes..., and set level 0, 1 and 2 to the _LOD_0/1/2 meshes.
3. Generate object LOD for the worldspace (in the Creation Kit or with xLODGen). The game only shows LOD from that generated data.
If you copy a vanilla LOD STAT (for example CambridgeBuilding05_LOD) and point it at your LOD mesh, the preview stays empty: those records have Is Marker ticked, and markers are not drawn.
Flat billboard LODs (_LOD_FLAT) are for trees: only two vanilla meshes use one, both maple trees. Buildings and props use real LOD meshes.
tags: lod object lod distant lod has distant lod specify distant lod meshes xlodgen stat lod_0 lod_1 lod_2 billboard is marker meshes\lod
verified_by: Scan of all 900 NIFs under Meshes\LOD in the unpacked vanilla Data folder (triangle counts, texture and material paths, shader flags 0x80000201/0x1, _LOD_FLAT count). Creation Kit test 2026-11-03: a STAT copied from CambridgeBuilding05_LOD showed an empty preview; setting the LOD meshes on the house STAT worked.

title: Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
content:
Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
Decimate removes triangles piece by piece. A model made of hundreds of thin separate pieces (tendrils, leaves, spikes, a building overgrown with plant meshes) breaks into floating shards at LOD triangle counts, and its silhouette disappears.
A better LOD for such models is one solid simplified skin: voxel-remesh the whole model, drop tiny loose bits, decimate that skin to the target count, UV-unwrap it and bake the original's colour and normal maps onto it. Measured on a 7,700-triangle overgrown house (outline overlap with the original from 12 views): solid skin 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.87 at 1,500 / 500 / 150 triangles, decimation 0.81 / 0.61 / 0.08.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5 does this by default (LOD generator, method Solid Shell): it writes _LOD_0/1/2 NIFs with their own baked textures (1K / 512 / 256) and .bgsm files under Meshes\LOD, Textures\LOD and Materials\LOD. Set its output folder to the mod's root folder (the one that holds Meshes and Textures); a folder inside the mod is cut back to the root automatically. Versions before 5.4.5 decimated, kept the full-size material and saved PNG textures the game cannot load.

title: Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
content:
Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
texconv treats a PNG or TGA as sRGB and, when writing a normal (UNORM) DDS format, converts it to linear. The result is visibly darker, and normal maps get distorted. Measured: a diffuse averaging 0.168 came out at 0.050; a normal map pixel (0.25, 0.5) came out at (0.05, 0.22).
Fix: add -srgb to the texconv command (texconv -y -f BC7_UNORM -srgb -o <folder> <file>). It keeps the values as they are, and the output format stays the same (DXT1, DXT5, BC5 and BC7_UNORM were checked). Converting DDS back to PNG is not affected.
The Mossy Blender add-on before 5.4.5 converted without -srgb, so textures it converted from PNG/TGA may be too dark and their normal maps off; convert or export them again with 5.4.5.
tags: texconv srgb dark darker texture dds conversion png tga normal map distorted bc7 bc5 dxt1 blender add-on
verified_by: Measured 2026-11-02 with the texconv shipped with FO4Edit 4.1.5q: mean pixel values of PNG -> DDS -> PNG round trips with and without -srgb, DDS header formats checked.

title: Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
content:
Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
A leaf card is a flat mesh whose diffuse texture's alpha channel cuts out the leaf shape. It needs the cutout and two-sided set in both places the game reads:
- In the NIF: a NiAlphaProperty with alpha test on (vanilla uses flags 4844 with a threshold around 127-128), and the shader's DOUBLE_SIDED flag.
- In the .bgsm: alpha test on with its threshold, and two-sided on. The .bgsm overrides the NIF, so if it has alpha test off the cutout does not show.
In Blender with PyNifly, a mesh loaded from a NIF uses PyNifly's own 'Fallout 4 MTS' shader group: textures are image nodes named Diffuse_Texture, Normal_Texture, Specular_Texture and Glow_Map_Texture feeding its Diffuse, Normal, Smooth Spec and Glow Map inputs. The cutout is the 'Alpha Property' node (Alpha Test on/off, Alpha Threshold 0-255), and PyNifly writes the NiAlphaProperty from it on export. The .bgsm path is the material property BSLSP_Shader_Name, and the shader flags are the Shader_Flags_1 / Shader_Flags_2 properties. Don't plug a Principled BSDF into such a material's output: that disconnects the NIF shader and its textures.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5's 'Set Up as Leaf Card' keeps the mesh's textures and material and adds all of this, including switching on alpha test and two-sided in the existing .bgsm (the original is kept as .bgsm.bak; game files are never edited).

verified_by: Vanilla ShackBalconyFloor01_LOD_0.nif NiAlphaProperty flags 4844 threshold 127 and ShackLOD01.BGSM alpha test on (read with PyNifly / the add-on's BGSM reader); PyNifly 27 shaders.blend group inputs and shader_io.py import/export code; leaf-card export of copies of MossShrub02 and Creosote01 compared with a plain export 2026-11-03.

title: Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
content:
Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
Two collision exports crash the Creation Kit:
1. Exact-mesh / building collision written by PyNifly (v27 and v28) as hknpCompressedMeshShape: PyNifly leaves the shape's search tree empty at every size, while all 167,285 vanilla compressed meshes have it filled. The CK crashes inside the Havok loader. Exporting that collision as a convex hull (up to 128 vertices) instead loads fine.
2. A building whose collision pieces are all bodies of one bhkPhysicsSystem, as PyNifly writes it: placing it crashes with 'Instance should have already been created' (bhknpcollisionobject.cpp line 611), because Havok rejects the physics data and the system ends up with no instance. Giving each piece its own single-body bhkPhysicsSystem loads fine; vanilla precombined meshes carry up to 590 such systems.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.4 fixed the first and 5.4.5 the second. Plain vanilla facts for reference: collision objects use flags 128, and BSXFlags 0x82 is the usual value for plants with collision.
If the crash continues after re-exporting, check that the Creation Kit is not still reading an older copy of the NIF from another mod in Mod Organizer.

verified_by: Vanilla scan of 167,285 compressed meshes and the multi-piece collision layout; CKPE crash dumps and CK disassembly of bhkNPCollisionObject::CreateInstance; Creation Kit tests 2026-11-02: a plant with collision and a 320-piece building (one system per piece) both load.

title: Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
content:
Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
Older versions of the Mossy Blender add-on (before 5.4.5) could print errors like AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type' from ui_panels.py in Blender's console, and a panel (for example LOD & Collision) failed to draw.
Cause: many of the add-on's tools register about 3 seconds after Blender starts (or on the first change to the scene). Until then Blender hands the panel nothing for those buttons, and the panel crashed setting an option on them. It is harmless: the error stops once those tools have loaded. If it keeps repeating long after start-up, the delayed tools failed to load; check Blender's system console (Window > Toggle System Console) for messages after 'Phase 2'.
Version 5.4.5 fixes it: the buttons always draw and get their options once the tools exist.

verified_by: Reproduced 2026-11-03 by drawing every panel in background Blender before the delayed tools registered: 7 panels failed before the fix, 0 after.

title: Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
content:
Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
Since version 5.4.5 every tool in the Mossy Blender add-on that touches a material only adds to what the mesh already has: material setup, Install Texture, Auto-Connect Textures, applying a .bgsm, Material Browser presets, Setup HD Material, Set Up as Leaf Card, joining meshes / Combine Vegetation, Apply Displacement and image import. Existing texture files are never written over when textures are copied or converted.
Older versions could, mostly on meshes loaded from a NIF: swap the material for an empty one, plug a new shader into the material output (the original textures were still in the node tree but no longer connected), delete the other materials after a join, turn leaves one-sided when a .bgsm was applied, or write over an existing .dds. If textures vanished after using one of those tools in an older version, open the Shader Editor: the original image nodes (Diffuse_Texture etc.) are often still there and can be reconnected, or reload the NIF.
Also fixed in 5.4.5: exporting had not created any new .bgsm files since 5.4.0 (existing ones were kept, new materials never got one).
Tools whose job is to put a new texture in a slot still do so when asked: Install Texture with a file you pick, Generate + Apply Texture, Wrap Image, baking AO into the diffuse, and picking a glow map. 'Mark as Collision Mesh' still clears that mesh's materials, as collision needs none.
